reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 35. Nay or No: 5. Not Voting: 0. Of 40 Yea or Nay votes where the Republican majority could be computed, 40 (100%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 210 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. Employer means where the donor works, not that the company gave money; corporations can't give directly to campaigns. Industry groups use simple keyword rules and may misclassify some donors.

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.
stands_for.scope: House roll calls 1–323 of 2026 (323 votes, January 6, 2026 to November 12, 2026), from the House Clerk.
stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.
stands_for.factual_flag: Not yet summarized: this line is built only from the official vote question and the bill's official title.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

posts.text:
Our nation’s veterans have selflessly served in defense of our freedoms, values, and country.

While today is a day to honor their steadfast service, I know that all of Nebraska joins in celebrating and cherishing their sacrifices and contributions yearlong. Happy #VeteransDay! https://t.co/GwsONPcYeY

Congrats to my good friend and colleague @Jim_Jordan on earning the support of @HouseGOP to become our next Minority Leader.

Jim is a longtime champion of conservative values. His leadership will help us hold the line and keep fighting for hardworking Americans.

Supporting our National Weather Service has been a priority of mine this Congress.

I'm glad to see this progress and will continue fighting to ensure the @NWS has the staffing and resources it needs to keep families safe across Nebraska and our country.
https://t.co/WaNYBpU0tT

Hardworking families shouldn’t pay more for prescriptions due to hidden fees and backroom deals.

Thanks to @HouseGOP legislation last year, this new rule will expose hidden PBM payments, increase price transparency, and finally help hold PBMs accountable.
https://t.co/a7GqjPAdUq

Strong infrastructure and safer roads are key to Lincoln’s continued growth.

I was glad to work with Mayor Gaylor Baird to secure $11.7 million in federal funding for key safety improvements along West O Street. More on this new grant and project here ⤵️
https://t.co/i5525ap2we

Joined the Bellevue Papillion Rotary Club this week to give an update on my work in Congress and on some of the projects bringing federal dollars back to Sarpy County.

Groups like this help Sarpy County continue to grow and thrive. Thanks for the invitation and for all you do! https://t.co/l0mAuEtron

Honored to welcome @NEAarts Chair Mary Anne Carter to Lincoln last week.

I enjoyed joining Chair Carter for a fireside chat on the importance of investing in the arts and highlighting Nebraska’s creative districts program, which supports local artists and communities statewide! https://t.co/osbecFeFlr

Rural communities know firsthand how crucial access to quality dialysis and kidney care is.

Happy to see @HHSGov start up this historic kidney care plan to improve care nationwide. I look forward to continuing our work to provide access to quality care!
https://t.co/MG3P73NWcY

The scene in Butler County is now secure following reports of an armed threat.

Thank you to Butler County law enforcement, @NEStatePatrol, and all first responders who jumped into action this morning to keep Nebraskans safe.
https://t.co/5ojvY0If7H

Stopped by for an overview of the Dari Processing construction site in Seward.

This investment in Seward will help boost Nebraska's growing dairy industry. Enjoyed the opportunity to learn more about the progress and prospects of this landmark milk processing facility! 🐄 https://t.co/pGEvPBzb8y

Glad to join the Seward County Rotary yesterday to share updates on my work in Congress and wins in bringing federal dollars back to the county.

Seward County’s strong business community and generosity help drive Nebraska’s economy and make it a great place to live and work! https://t.co/8FQyqApQic

Great to join @SCCNeb today as @GEICO donated two vehicles to its Auto Collision Repair Technology Program in Milford.

These vehicles will help train the next generation of technicians on modern vehicle safety systems, sensors, and electronics. Thanks again to @GEICO! https://t.co/TEzCzK1pYS

Honored to speak at and take questions from @nwas during their 51st Annual Meeting in Omaha.

The weather enterprise plays a crucial role in keeping families safe, protecting our communities, and supporting farmers and ranchers nationwide. Always thankful for their dedication! https://t.co/q6GSADBShU

Foreign dollars are driving up insurance costs and more by bankrolling costly litigation cases in American courts.

Last month, I asked @SecScottBessent about this and was glad to hear his support.

Good to see @NRO shine a light on this growing issue ⤵️
https://t.co/R4jVIkBv54

Bipartisanship can be hard to find in Washington, yet @RepLiccardo and I are working together to find meaningful solutions to our housing crisis.

Was more than glad to join him for @BretBaier’s latest 'Common Ground' segment yesterday to detail our work on @FinancialCmte 👇 https://t.co/vslLqIFmOR

My family knows firsthand the strength that comes from the prayers of others in the fight against cancer.

Please join me and billions of faithful around the world in praying for strength and healing for Pope Leo. https://t.co/x0oVvkUktO

Happy to join @SarpyCounty Chamber yesterday to detail housing affordability, federal funding I've helped secure, my priorities in Congress, and more.

As Nebraska’s fastest-growing county, local families and small businesses are set to thrive even more with these wins! https://t.co/EMHtthgpsu

Rural lawyers represent the very best of the profession.

Julie Bear of Plattsmouth repeatedly lives up to that.

Serving with distinction as a public defender for Cass County, Julie has consistently demonstrated her ability to deliver for clients in criminal defense and beyond. https://t.co/P3YPD2PlfR

More on this historic milestone ⤵️
https://t.co/OYks6GUet2

Today marks 100 days since we finalized trade talks with the European Union. Our ag exports to the EU are already up 17% this year.

Republicans have renegotiated our trade deals to level the playing field, and our deal with the EU shows that it's working. Just look at the https://t.co/OPiyLO61Q7

Rural lawyers represent the very best of the profession.

Norfolk’s Bre Flaherty is a great example.

From the Platte County Attorney’s Office to now serving as County Court Judge in the Fifth Judicial District, Bre’s career reflects her focus on community service and integrity. https://t.co/FiuYHuAPGx

Stopped by @wpcadets last week to talk with students about Congress, civic engagement, and more.

Always appreciate the opportunity to hear from Nebraska’s next generation and to see the talent and enthusiasm of the Cadets! https://t.co/eSnRTzdxlj

.@HouseGOP has a story to tell with our wins for hardworking families:

💰No taxes on tips and overtime
🚫 No taxes on Social Security for most seniors
🏡 Landmark housing legislation
🧑‍🧑‍🧒‍🧒 Child tax credit increased

... and much, much more! https://t.co/ji4btyCvSo

Recently toured Nebraska Gas Turbine in Hooper to learn more about their work in aviation, maintenance, repair, and more.

Businesses like this showcase the innovation, skilled workforce, and entrepreneurial spirit that continue to set Nebraska apart! https://t.co/5KH6hGYQpp

Rural lawyers represent the very best of the profession.

This week, I’m highlighting the impact they have on their communities, starting with Fremont’s Shane Placek and his remarkable work in domestic law.

Shane's skill and tenacity earn respect from clients and judges alike ⤵️ https://t.co/6uvhfrvP1K

Great to visit Guardian Angels Central Catholic High School and talk with their students about civics, Congress, public service, and more!

GACC is doing great work preparing Nebraska’s next generation to lead and serve their communities. https://t.co/07frjY8WRr

Glad to join Mayor Hike, State Senator Rountree, and other leaders in Bellevue for an update on their indoor waterpark, which is set to be the first @Mattel Wonder Indoor Waterpark.

Bellevue is growing, and attractions like this will help fuel even more economic success! https://t.co/Ei5lr06bDo

Karly Rain Wood lost her life to a four-time convicted felon. This happens far too often.

I am happy to lead the House version of the Karly Rain Wood Act to create a public registry for repeat violent offenders and help stop this cycle.

Read more here ➡️ https://t.co/PJSOlMd1ld https://t.co/r9oCwdh5Dm

My team and I continue to monitor the flooding across southeast Nebraska that began overnight.

Please stay alert, stay safe, and continue to follow the National Weather Service for the latest updates. https://t.co/VkMZgg5otC

Recently met with Papillion Mayor @dpblack and Police Chief Chris Whitted to tour the @papillionpolice Station’s expansion and renovations.

Happy to see these projects move along, especially as Papillion continues to grow and thrive. Thanks for the tour and great conversation! https://t.co/WTO7JLnGAt

Want to make an impact on Capitol Hill?

Our interns get to engage with constituent services, communications, legislation, committee work, and more from my D.C. office!

The deadline is quickly approaching – be sure to share and apply by October 2nd TODAY👉https://t.co/viVnPSsrMs https://t.co/G179toIJQQ
Live now on @cspan!  ⤵️ https://t.co/AndG2i9RId

Today marked the final Nebraska Breakfast of 2026– and the last one with @RepDonBacon!

My team and I were happy to host the Breakfast in its 83rd year, bringing Nebraskans visiting DC together with our federal delegation. Thanks to everyone who helped keep this tradition alive. https://t.co/g2F2dzoCAB

Stablecoins will play a huge role in the future of digital assets – and can be a powerful tool to strengthen the US dollar.

With the GENIUS Act now law, I asked @SecScottBessent about getting rule making right and ensuring America leads during this era of crypto innovation 👇 https://t.co/WSfgc7gkjH

Today marks 25 years since September 11th, 2001.

On this solemn anniversary, we honor the thousands of lives lost and the courageous first responders who stepped up without hesitation. Their sacrifice will never be forgotten. 🇺🇸 https://t.co/AASnixgsjG

The same right to free speech that protects appalling posters like these also protected Charlie Kirk's right to free speech.

It is disturbing that a growing number of young people believe speech they don't like should be met with violence. That's un-American and unacceptable. https://t.co/Egb6YzQsvF

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
